    [4, 5, 7, 5, 9, 2, 3, 1, 7, 8, 6, 9, 4, 2, 4, 2, 5, 1, 2, 7],
    [9, 1, 7, 5, 5, 1, 2, 7, 1, 9, 1, 7, 4, 8, 4, 7, 2, 9, 5, 8],
    [9, 1, 8, 6, 9, 4, 7, 6, 9, 5, 5, 5, 8, 1, 4, 8, 4, 7, 8, 5],
    [4, 2, 9, 5, 5, 2, 8, 2, 7, 7, 9, 6, 1, 4, 9, 8, 3, 3, 9, 2],
    [1, 9, 2, 3, 8, 4, 3, 1, 1, 3, 4, 6, 3, 5, 1, 1, 2, 6, 4, 6],
    [1, 4, 3, 5, 6, 1, 1, 1, 1, 6, 7, 3, 9, 5, 8, 3, 5, 6, 2, 9],
    [7, 7, 1, 9, 2, 4, 6, 9, 1, 5, 5, 8, 5, 2, 2, 2, 4, 2, 1, 2],
    [2, 9, 6, 1, 2, 9, 4, 8, 2, 7, 8, 2, 5, 7, 3, 2, 2, 4, 7, 7],
    [4, 2, 6, 6, 8, 9, 2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 5, 8, 3, 7, 4, 8, 5, 2, 1],
    [3, 2, 4, 8, 9, 8, 9, 5, 2, 1, 6, 8, 1, 2, 5, 7, 9, 1, 8, 5],
    [1, 3, 7, 2, 7, 3, 5, 2, 3, 9, 3, 2, 7, 2, 1, 7, 9, 8, 5, 7],
    [1, 6, 4, 6, 6, 5, 5, 9, 2, 3, 2, 4, 6, 7, 3, 9, 9, 9, 6, 6],
    [8, 6, 5, 2, 2, 3, 2, 1, 4, 9, 6, 9, 4, 9, 7, 7, 1, 5, 9, 3],
    [3, 7, 7, 5, 9, 8, 7, 4, 2, 2, 9, 5, 0, 0, 8, 6, 7, 6, 6, 7],
    [6, 9, 5, 6, 3, 7, 5, 7, 9, 8, 9, 5, 0, 0, 4, 2, 3, 3, 2, 6],
    [2, 8, 5, 3, 5, 6, 7, 1, 4, 7, 4, 4, 9, 5, 1, 3, 4, 4, 4, 7],
    [7, 8, 4, 7, 9, 5, 7, 8, 7, 4, 6, 8, 5, 3, 3, 1, 4, 1, 9, 7],
    [4, 5, 9, 9, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9, 8, 5, 8, 8, 6, 2, 8, 3, 7, 2, 4],
    [1, 6, 1, 4, 3, 6, 5, 4, 1, 7, 4, 7, 8, 6, 5, 9, 5, 4, 9, 9],
    [2, 9, 2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 9, 6, 4, 5, 8, 7, 5, 4, 3, 6, 3, 9, 5],
]

def test_candidate(cand):
    new_grid = [row[:] for row in input_grid]
    new_grid[13][12] = cand[0][0]
    new_grid[13][13] = cand[0][1]
    new_grid[14][12] = cand[1][0]
    new_grid[14][13] = cand[1][1]
    
    s13 = len(set(new_grid[13]))
    s14 = len(set(new_grid[14]))
    s12 = len(set(new_grid[r][12] for r in range(20)))
    s13 = len(set(new_grid[r][13] for r in range(20)))
    
    return s13, s14, s12, s13

# Search all 10000 possibilities, find best
import itertools

best_score = -1
best_c = None
all_results = []

for c in itertools.product(range(10), repeat=4):
    s13, s14, s12, s13_2 = test_candidate([[c[0], c[1]], [c[2], c[3]]])
    score = s13 + s14 + s12 + s13_2  # higher is better
    all_results.append((score, c))

# Sort by score descending
all_results.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)

print("Top 20 candidates (score = sum of unique counts):")
for score, c in all_results[:20]:
    print(f"  {c}: score {score}")

# Check if any candidate achieves 40 (all rows and cols have 10 unique)
perfect = [(s, c) for s, c in all_results if s == 40]
print(f"\nPerfect candidates (score=40): {len(perfect)}")

# Check candidates with specific row/col patterns
print("\n\nCandidates satisfying row uniqueness constraints:")
for score, c in all_results:
    if c[0] == 1 or c[1] == 1 or c[2] == 1 or c[3] == 1:
        cand = [[c[0], c[1]], [c[2], c[3]]]
        s13, s14, s12, s13_2 = test_candidate(cand)
        if s13 == 10 and s14 == 10:
            print(f"  {cand}: rows 13,14 both have 10 unique (score={score})")

# Check column 12 constraint (needs 2)
print("\n\nChecking column 12 for value 2:")
for score, c in all_results:
    if c[0] == 2 or c[2] == 2:
        cand = [[c[0], c[1]], [c[2], c[3]]]
        s13, s14, s12, s13_2 = test_candidate(cand)
        if s12 == 10:
            print(f"  {cand}: cols 12 has 10 unique (score={score})")

# What if the constraint is different? Like each row should have exactly one duplicate?
# Let me check the duplicate pattern
print("\n\nLooking for candidates with specific duplicate pattern:")
for score, c in all_results[:50]:
    cand = [[c[0], c[1]], [c[2], c[3]]]
    s13, s14, s12, s13_2 = test_candidate(cand)
    if c[0] == c[1] == c[2] == c[3]:
        print(f"  {cand}: all same (score={score})")

# Try diagonal patterns like [[2,0],[0,2]] or [[1,2],[2,1]]
diag_candidates = [
    [[2, 1], [1, 0]], [[2, 0], [0, 1]], [[1, 2], [2, 0]], [[1, 0], [0, 2]]
]

print("\n\nTesting diagonal candidates:")
for cand in diag_candidates:
    s13, s14, s12, s13_2 = test_candidate(cand)
    print(f"  {cand}: rows 13={s13}, 14={s14}, cols 12={s12}, 13={s13_2}")
